messages:
sam (support): Heads-up — ACME reached out asking for a hard increase to their per-minute token limit. They say traffic spike due to a promotional campaign. They want 10x for 48h and then reassess.
priya (sales): Customer is on standard tier. They pushed this through yesterday, urgent for their launch. They offered to sign an addendum if needed.
maya (product): @sam can you paste the request details? we need expected qps, peak tokens/min, example payloads, and whether this is user-generated content or automated crawlers.
sam (support): Copying the note from ACME: "We expect 75 requests/s at ~2k tokens avg = ~9M tokens/min. Burst window ~30 minutes. Use-case: personalized recommendations via LLM, user-driven. Will sign an addendum. Contact: dana@acme.com"
alex (eng-sre): 9M tokens/min on standard tier is risky. We need rate history and API key, account ID, and any IP ranges. Also want to check for abnormal pattern (sudden ramp vs steady).
jordan (ops): Also need to know if they plan to open multiple API keys or reuse one. If it's single key we can gate with more granular token caps.
fraud-bot: Alert: account ACME-312 flagged for "rapid key churn" 2 weeks ago. Similar behavior patterns previously linked to automated scraping. Confidence: 0.62
priya (sales): That flag is surprising — customer claims legitimate. They passed initial KYC during procurement. I'll ask for a contact call and product demo that shows intended flow.
maya (product): OK — here's what I propose for triage and routing to product backlog vs emergency allowance: 1) short-term: approve a temporary, monitored capacity bump (48h) with throttles and token caps per key + mandatory webhook for usage telemetry. 2) medium-term: create a backlog ticket to evaluate if this traffic pattern should be supported as a new capacity offering (Dedicated or burst add-on). Acceptance criteria in backlog ticket: reproducible perf under requested QPS, cost/per-token estimate, safety/fraud checklist, rollback plan, and SLA-adjusted pricing.
sam (support): For short-term we need exact controls we can set. alex — can you enumerate the config?
alex (eng-sre): We can do: - token_limit_per_min = 10M - concurrent_requests = 200 - require per-key burst window 30m - enable monitoring webhook to customer-managed endpoint + alert to ops channel if >85% of token_limit. We also need to add a temporary rule to automatically scale down if error rate >2% or latency >1.5s p95.
priya (sales): Customer agrees to webhook and monitoring. They asked if we can avoid a Dedicated contract. They prefer a temporary boost.
maya (product): Good. For the backlog ticket please include these acceptance criteria: - run perf test simulating 75 rps, 2k tokens avg for 30m - no regressions on p95 latency under 1.5s on current runtime config - cost delta estimate and suggested pricing (sales to help) - fraud review completed and documented - launch checklist: rollout plan (canary 10% -> 30% -> 100%), observability dashboards added, and rollback knob.
jordan (ops): Add mandatory logs to ticket: sample request IDs for tracing, IP ranges, auth key hash (never raw keys). Also add contact for emergency kill switch (pager or slack).
sam (support): I'll ask ACME for the test payload and IPs, and request they sign a temporary terms addendum.
fraud-bot: Suggestion: require at least one day of pre-approval monitoring with limits at 20% of request, to verify behavior.
priya (sales): ACME pushed back on delay — launch is in 24h. They need 48h full capacity.
maya (product): Tradeoffs: immediate full bump risks abuse + capacity pressure. Mitigation we can accept: a staged increase w/ escrowed metrics — i.e., grant 48h 100% but with enforced token caps per minute and automated kill if fraud signals exceed threshold. We should document rollback and financial exposure.
alex (eng-sre): I can implement automated kill rules tied to fraud-bot signals (if churn or abnormal session replay >0.5) and to error/latency thresholds. Also we'll enable more aggressive prefix/KV cache eviction to protect other tenants.
jordan (ops): I'll prepare a temporary runbook with steps to revert, and a Slack alert playbook.
maya (product): Ok action items: 1) sam to get test payloads, IPs, and signed addendum from ACME (deadline: +2h) 2) alex to stage throttles and kill switches in a config branch and share sandbox command snippet 3) priyato confirm pricing addendum draft 4) jordan to author runbook 5) maya to create a product backlog ticket for long-term capacity offering and link to this thread.
sam (support): On it. sending ACME the form now.
alex (eng-sre): sandbox command snippet (example):
```
# temp quota rule
apply_quota --account=ACME-312 --tokens_per_min=10000000 --burst_window=1800 --concurrent_reqs=200 --kill_on_metrics='error_rate>0.02||p95_latency>1.5'
```
priya (sales): :thumbsup: will push pricing draft to dana and ask for immediate signature.
maya (product): If we get signed addendum and test payloads within 2h we approve the 48h boost with the mitigations above. Otherwise default to staged 20% trial.
fraud-bot: Monitoring enabled. Will post anomalies to #ops-alerts if thresholds tripped.
sam (support): Update: ACME provided test payload and agreed to addendum, signed PDF attached in ticket.
maya (product): Thanks — alex/jordan please proceed with deployment and post rollout timeframe here. I'll create backlog ticket and paste its ID once done.
alex (eng-sre): Deployed throttles to staging, will promote to prod in 15m assuming smoke checks pass.
jordan (ops): Runbook live at https://confluence/redwood/ops/runbooks/acme-temp-boost (access: ops + oncall).
maya (product): Backlog ticket created: PROD-1827. It contains AC acceptance criteria and links. Leaving this thread open for updates. :eyes:
